properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"yes, close the contradiction explicitly. go with your recommendation."*

═══ THE CONTRADICTION, AND WHY IT COULD NOT BE LEFT ═══

`dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` — **ACCEPTED 2026-07-31** — forbids a written orientation document: *"NO START-HERE FILE... a START-HERE.md is `dev_storyflow` in miniature — it would go stale, and STALENESS IN AN ORIENTATION DOCUMENT IS THE WORST PLACE FOR IT."* `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents` says the same as a standing rule.

`.claude/handoff_nudge.py` — **committed 2026-07-23**, eight days earlier — blocked the agent from ending a working session until it wrote exactly such a document into `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`. **Machine-local, uncommitted, invisible to every reflow2 tool.** Nobody reconciled them for five weeks.

Anthony reached the same conclusion independently on 2026-08-26, from TRANSPORTABILITY rather than staleness: *"I'm not a fan of markdown files... I'm not sure that handoff documents are transportable to different machines (especially if they are stored as memory and are not committed)."* He has a second box (`ajs77`); the note did not exist on it.

═══ THE RESOLUTION ═══

**① The hook is RETIRED.** `.claude/handoff_nudge.py` deleted and its two registrations removed from `.claude/settings.json` (SessionStart and Stop). `tools/loop_nudge.py` is untouched and keeps all four of its registrations — that one enforces the coherence loop, which is computed from graph state and contradicts nothing.

**② `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` STANDS UNCHANGED, and its scope is now stated.** It governs ORIENTATION — *"what is this project about, and what does it owe?"* — and that question is answered by `where-am-i`, `what_next`, `loop_status` and `cap:onboarding`, all built. It was never narrowed to make room for the hook; the hook was simply wrong.

**③ THE EXOGENOUS HALF ALREADY HAS A HOME, AND IT IS `TemporalFact`.** This is the part that makes the retirement safe rather than lossy, and it needed no new vocabulary. A handoff note carries two things:

- **Transient state** — *"CI was pending when I stopped"*, *"#345 is a green draft"*. Genuinely ephemeral, and already answerable from `loop_status`, `gh pr checks` and the forge. Writing it down was always a retelling.
- **Durable traps** — *"`gh pr edit` is broken, use `gh api -X PATCH`"*, *"a piped gate returns the wrong exit code"*, *"`--stop-shared` leaks a zombie"*. **These are dated observations about the world, which is exactly what a TemporalFact is**, and the design already carries dozens of them: `fact:the-stale-daemon-cost-five-merged-prs-twice`, `fact:defect-agents-md-said-an-mcp-reconnect-picks-up-a-rebuild-and-a-shared-server-makes-that-false`, `fact:the-target-dir-reached-263-gib-of-this-projects-own-test-binaries`.

⭐ **So the most valuable content of every handoff note was already being written to the graph in parallel, in the right node type, by sessions that also wrote it to a markdown file nobody else could read.** The retirement does not lose it; it stops duplicating it into a place the design cannot see.

═══ THE COST, STATED ═══

⚠️ **Nothing now blocks a session from ending without recording what it learned.** The hook's one real virtue was that it was unavoidable, and this session is evidence that unavoidable works — `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` held tonight precisely because it stopped the build, while four other rules were broken by an agent that had them available and never opened them.

The honest position is that this trades an enforced-but-wrong mechanism for a correct-but-unenforced one, and **that is a real regression on the enforcement axis**. It is accepted because a mechanism that writes to one laptop was never going to survive the second machine, let alone a consumer. Whether the TemporalFact route needs its own trigger is left open and belongs with `dec:idea-a-hotspot-node-holds-the-live-worklist-and-is-deliberately-not-history`, which asks where a working set lives at all.

📌 **A consumer copying reflow2's example would have copied the contradiction** — the hook shipped in `.claude/`, which the installer's neighbours read. That is `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` applying to the repo's own furniture.
properties.name: DECIDED — the handoff hook is retired: orientation is computed, durable traps are TemporalFacts, and no markdown document carries either
properties.rationale:
Settled by Anthony on 2026-08-26 after the contradiction was put to him with both sides named. He chose to close it rather than let either side quietly win, which was the recommendation.

The decision retires the hook rather than narrowing the accepted decision, because the accepted decision is right and the hook was wrong: it enforced a document whose staleness was the original objection AND whose location made it untransportable, so it failed on both the axis it was argued against and the axis it was never tested on.

The TemporalFact observation is what makes this cheap. It was found by looking at what the memory notes actually contained and noticing the durable half was already in the graph under the right type — so the resolution required no new vocabulary, no new node type, and no build. The enforcement regression is written in rather than glossed, because trading an unavoidable mechanism for a voluntary one is a real loss and a later reader should meet it rather than discover it.
